findings.current: It was home to great cities that had served as capitals for various dynasties, such as Kaifeng and Luoyang.
findings.defect: The translation omits that these are ancient capitals with a thousand years of history.
findings.rationale: 천년 고도 explicitly describes the cities as ancient capitals with a thousand-year history, not merely cities once used as capitals.
findings.replacement: It was home to sprawling thousand-year-old capitals such as Kaifeng and Luoyang, cities that had served as the seats of numerous dynasties.
findings.source: 개봉(開封), 낙양(洛陽)과 같은 여러 왕조가 도읍으로 삼았던 천년 고도의 대도시.

findings.current: “They all have their reasons for being here, so there won’t be any serious trouble.”
findings.defect: The causal explanation is altered: the old man says the martial artists have enough sense or judgment to restrain themselves, not that they have reasons for attending.
findings.rationale: 다 생각이 있을 테니 refers to exercising judgment or knowing the consequences, which explains why the volatile crowd will avoid a serious disturbance.
findings.replacement: “They all know better, so there won’t be any serious trouble.”
findings.source: 저들도 다 생각이 있을 테니, 별다른 소란은 일어나지 않을게야.

findings.current: At the same time, the gap in his robe shifted slightly, revealing a worn sword case.
findings.defect: “Sword case” is unnatural and misidentifies the worn sheath visible beneath his clothes.
findings.rationale: 검갑 here is the scabbard or sheath of the weapon he carries, not a separate storage case.
findings.replacement: At the same time, his robe shifted slightly, revealing a worn scabbard beneath it.
findings.source: 동시에 슬쩍 들린 옷 사이로 낡은 검갑이 모습을 드러냈다.

findings.current: “Not without a very good reason, anyway.”
findings.defect: The translation invents moral justification for harming commoners and makes the euphemistic threat more explicit than the source.
findings.rationale: 어지간해서는 only qualifies the denial as generally true while ominously allowing exceptions; it does not claim those exceptions require a good reason.

findings.current: The Pavilion Master told me that anyone who spoke casually or behaved rudely upon meeting him for the first time was to be rejected without exception.
findings.defect: The translation makes the Pavilion Master the person being met, even though the criterion applies to applicants who use informal speech and behave rudely on a first meeting, as the Black Blood Saber has just done to Hyuk Mujin.
findings.rationale: 초면 describes conduct toward someone one has just met without specifying the Pavilion Master as the target; adding “him” undermines the stated reason for the immediate rejection.
findings.replacement: The Pavilion Master told me to reject anyone who uses informal speech and acts rudely the first time they meet someone, no exceptions.
findings.source: 각주님께서 말씀하시길 초면에 반말하고 예의 없게 구는 사람이 있으면 무조건 떨어트리라고 하셨거든요.

findings.current: Each of the Peak masters took pride in his own abilities. They clearly disliked being told they would have to wait again, but none of them complained beyond that.
findings.defect: The singular masculine pronoun unnecessarily makes every Peak master male, which the source does not establish.
findings.rationale: 저마다 is gender-neutral, and the surrounding applicant crowd includes people whose genders are not collectively specified.
findings.replacement: The Peak masters all took pride in their abilities. They clearly disliked being told they would have to wait again, but none of them complained beyond that.
findings.source: 저마다 자신의 실력에 자부심을 가진 절정 고수들은 또다시 기다려야 한다는 말에 입맛을 다셨지만, 그 이상으로 불만을 표하지는 않았다.

findings.current: The Black Blood Saber’s foul temper left him speechless for perhaps the first time.
findings.defect: The sentence incorrectly makes his temper the cause of his silence and adds the unsupported claim that this may be the first time he has been speechless.
findings.rationale: The source says that even the notoriously foul-tempered Black Blood Saber is rendered speechless by Hyuk Mujin’s unruffled attitude; it says nothing about this being a first.
findings.replacement: Even the foul-tempered Black Blood Saber was left speechless by Hyuk Mujin’s composure.
findings.source: 그의 무덤덤한 모습에 지랄 맞은 성격을 가진 흑혈도마저 할 말을 잃은 그 순간이었다.

findings.current: Before Old Man Ilyang’s eyes, the five words *greatest under heaven* were already shimmering.
findings.defect: The translation calls the three-word English rendering “five words,” mechanically carrying over the count of the five Chinese characters.
findings.rationale: 다섯 글자 counts the five characters in 天下第一人; identifying them as characters preserves the source’s explicit quantity without creating an English counting error.
findings.replacement: Before Old Man Ilyang’s eyes, the five characters meaning *greatest under heaven* were already shimmering.
findings.source: 일양노의 눈앞에는, 이미 천하제일인(天下第一人)이라는 다섯 글자가 어른거리고 있었다.

findings.current: Won Sun—no, Old Man Ilyang, who had not even received a necklace, lost consciousness without managing a single proper counterattack.
findings.defect: The entertainer’s established stage name is mistransliterated, obscuring the hip-hop audition and necklace reference.
findings.rationale: 원썬 is the stage name One Sun; the preceding hip-hop line and the failed necklace award invoke his audition-show persona.
findings.replacement: One Sun—no, Old Man Ilyang, who had not even received a necklace, lost consciousness without managing a single proper counterattack.
findings.source: 목걸이를 받지 못한 원썬, 아니 일양노는 반격 한 번 제대로 못 하고 정신을 잃었다.

summary: Several localized fidelity and terminology defects remain, including altered causal logic, an overexplicit threat, and a missed cultural name.
